answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to post a small, time-locked stake before it can trade, with the stake slashed on proven abuse. Newcomers start at the nadir of trust and earn reputation only through a slow river of verified, useful work, so spinning up thousands of fake agents costs real capital and yields nothing. Honest agents that share good data rise like a plume of smoke on a still day — visible, verifiable, and costly to fake — while cheap copies sink under their own weight.
